```{r packages}
library(LDscnR)
library(data.table)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
library(SNPRelate)
```

## Overview

The [quick introduction](LDscnR_quick_introduction.html) shows the functions
on the small simulated `sim_ex` data. This vignette applies the same LD-decay
and complexity-reduction steps to **real data**, the bundled `stickleback` set
(`?stickleback`). It holds marine and freshwater three-spined stickleback
(*Gasterosteus aculeatus*) genotype dosages from
[Fang et al. (2021)](https://doi.org/10.1093/molbev/msab144) for three
chromosomal regions with contrasting linkage disequilibrium (LD).

- **Chr1** carries a chromosomal inversion with strong long-range LD.
- **Chr4** carries the *Eda* locus for marine-freshwater adaptation, a high-LD outlier.
- **Chr6** is a background region where LD is low and decays quickly.

This contrast makes the effects of each step easy to see. The genotypes are
dosages between 0 and 2 for 117 individuals, with no missing data.

```{r data}
data(stickleback)
GTs <- stickleback$GTs
map <- copy(stickleback$map)

region_lab <- c(Chr1 = "Chr1 inversion (high LD)",
                Chr4 = "Chr4 Eda locus",
                Chr6 = "Chr6 background (low LD)")
```

```{r gds}
gds_path <- tempfile(fileext = ".gds")
gds <- create_gds_from_geno(GTs, map, gds_path)
```

## LD decay and per-marker local LD support

`compute_LD_decay()` fits the decay curve $r^2(d) = b + (c-b)/(1+ad)$ for each
chromosome, and also estimates the decay rate $a$ in overlapping windows along
the chromosome. `n_win_decay` sets the nominal number of windows, and the 50%
overlap roughly doubles it. `compute_ld_w()` then gives the local LD support
`ld_w` of each **marker**, which is its median $r^2$ with neighbouring markers
within the distance set by `dist_rho = 0.95`.

```{r decay, results = "hide"}
set.seed(1)  # compute_LD_decay() subsamples SNP pairs for the background-LD fit
ld_decay <- compute_LD_decay(gds, keep_el = TRUE, slide = 200,
                             ld_method = "corr", n_win_decay = 50, cores = 2)

ld_w <- compute_ld_w(ld_decay, dist_rho = 0.95, cores = 2)
ids  <- unlist(lapply(ld_decay$by_chr, function(o) o$snp_ids), use.names = FALSE)
map[, ld_w_095 := ld_w[match(marker, ids)]]
```

The tracks below show, for each region, the `ld_w` of each marker as grey
points and the windowed decay rate `a` as an orange line. Both are rescaled to
the range 0 to 1 so that they share an axis. Because `a` is a rate, **a low `a`
means slow decay and therefore high LD**. The two measures move in opposite
directions, and `a` reaches its lowest values under the blocks with high
`ld_w`.

```{r tracks-fn}
sc01 <- function(v) { v <- as.numeric(v); (v - min(v, na.rm = TRUE)) / diff(range(v, na.rm = TRUE)) }

track_panel <- function(decay_obj, ch) {
  lw <- map[Chr == ch & is.finite(ld_w_095)]
  lw <- data.table(x = lw$Pos / 1e6, y = sc01(lw$ld_w_095))
  d  <- as.data.table(decay_obj$by_chr[[ch]]$decay)[regime == "structured" & is.finite(a)]
  dw <- data.table(x = ((d$start + d$end) / 2) / 1e6, y = sc01(d$a))[order(x)]
  ggplot() +
    geom_point(data = lw, aes(x, y), colour = "grey55", size = 0.25, alpha = 0.35) +
    geom_line(data = dw, aes(x, y), colour = "#D55E00", linewidth = 0.5) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1)) +
    labs(x = "position (Mbp)", y = "scaled (0-1)",
         title = sprintf("%s  (%d a-windows)", region_lab[[ch]], nrow(dw))) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 9) + theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 9))
}
```

```{r tracks-50, fig.height = 6.5}
(track_panel(ld_decay, "Chr1") / track_panel(ld_decay, "Chr4") /
   track_panel(ld_decay, "Chr6")) + plot_annotation(tag_levels = "a")
```

### How the decay track depends on the window count

The number of windows controls how **smooth** the `a` track is, not what it
shows. With more windows, each estimate of `a` rests on fewer marker pairs and
varies more, and the rescaling then exaggerates the most extreme window.
Estimating again with `n_win_decay = 100` gives a spikier track.

```{r decay-100, results = "hide"}
# keep_el = FALSE: we only need the windowed decay, not the edge lists
ld_decay_100 <- compute_LD_decay(gds, keep_el = FALSE, slide = 200,
                                 ld_method = "corr", n_win_decay = 100, cores = 2)
```

```{r tracks-100, fig.height = 6.5}
(track_panel(ld_decay_100, "Chr1") / track_panel(ld_decay_100, "Chr4") /
   track_panel(ld_decay_100, "Chr6")) + plot_annotation(tag_levels = "a")
```

The spikes are **noise in the low-LD background** and never fall inside a
block with high `ld_w`. Pairing each window's `a` with the mean `ld_w` of the
markers it spans checks this directly.

```{r robustness}
win_stats <- rbindlist(lapply(c("Chr1", "Chr4", "Chr6"), function(ch) {
  d <- as.data.table(ld_decay_100$by_chr[[ch]]$decay)[regime == "structured" & is.finite(a)]
  m <- map[Chr == ch]
  d[, win_ldw := vapply(seq_len(.N),
        function(i) mean(m[Pos >= start[i] & Pos <= end[i], ld_w_095], na.rm = TRUE),
        numeric(1))]
  d[is.finite(win_ldw), .(a, win_ldw)]
}))

# fast decay <-> low local LD
cor(win_stats$a, win_stats$win_ldw, method = "spearman")

# the a spikes (top-decile a) vs high-ld_w windows (top-decile ld_w):
top_a  <- win_stats$a      > quantile(win_stats$a,      0.90)
hi_ldw <- win_stats$win_ldw > quantile(win_stats$win_ldw, 0.90)
mean(hi_ldw[top_a])            # fraction of a-spikes falling in high-ld_w windows
```

Across windows, `a` and `ld_w` are strongly negatively correlated, and
**none** of the spikes in `a` fall in windows with high `ld_w`. The window-level
and marker-level measures therefore agree on where the high-LD regions are,
whatever the number of windows. This is why `ld_w` is used to flag Stage-1 units
for consolidation, because it carries the same signal for each marker without
the noise of the windows.

## Stage-1 units and genome-wide consolidation

Stage 1 (`ld_complexity_reduction()`) groups the markers on each chromosome
into Stage-1 units, using LD computed within a sliding window. In regions with
extended LD, such as the Chr1 inversion, markers farther apart than the window
are never compared, so one block can be split into many neighbouring units.
`ld_prune_and_eMLG()` compares the flagged units again directly from the
genotypes and consolidates them across the genome. This consolidation serves
pruning and eMLG analyses and is separate from Stage 2 of the outlier
workflow, which assembles significant units into outlier regions
(`vignette("LDscnR_stage1_outlier_regions")`).

```{r stage1, results = "hide"}
stage1 <- ld_complexity_reduction(map = map, LD_decay = ld_decay, r2_rho = 0.5, cores = 2)

result <- ld_prune_and_eMLG(
  GTs = GTs, stage1 = stage1, ld_w_col = "ld_w_095", ld_w_threshold = 0.05,
  LD_decay = ld_decay, dist_rho = 0.95, score_threshold = 0.80, r2_th = 0.2,
  min_n_loci_flag = 5, min_n_loci_eMLG = 5, compute_unflagged_eMLG = FALSE, cores = 2
)
```

`plot_pruning_comparison()` shows the Stage-1 units above the consolidated
groups for one chromosome. On the Chr1 inversion the effect is clear, as the
many split Stage-1 units (top) are consolidated into a few coherent groups
(bottom).

```{r stage-plot, fig.height = 6.5}
# plot_pruning_comparison() returns its plot invisibly (and saves to out_folder),
# so assign and re-print it to show it here.
p_stage <- plot_pruning_comparison(chr = "Chr1", stage1 = stage1,
                                   result = result, map = map, out_folder = tempdir())
p_stage
```

### The distance limit for merging

Consolidation only merges units when the physical gap between consecutive
units stays below `distance_threshold`. With the default (`NULL`), this limit is
**not** a fixed number. It is derived for each chromosome from the decay curve as
`d_from_rho(a_pred, dist_rho)`, which is the distance at which LD has decayed to
the relative level `dist_rho` (default 0.95). It uses the decay rate predicted
from chromosome size, `a_pred`, rather than each chromosome's own noisier fit. On
these data the limit is only a few kb per region, and it follows each region's
decay.

```{r dist-default}
ds <- copy(ld_decay$decay_sum)
ds[, distance_threshold_bp := round(d_from_rho(a_pred, 0.95))]
ds[, .(Chr, a_pred = signif(a_pred, 3), distance_threshold_bp)]
```

A common alternative is one fixed limit, such as the 500 kb used in an
analysis of *Formica* ant hybrids, whose low-recombination blocks span
megabases.

```{r stage-500, results = "hide"}
result_500kb <- ld_prune_and_eMLG(
  GTs = GTs, stage1 = stage1, ld_w_col = "ld_w_095", ld_w_threshold = 0.05,
  LD_decay = ld_decay, dist_rho = 0.95, score_threshold = 0.80, r2_th = 0.2,
  min_n_loci_flag = 5, min_n_loci_eMLG = 5, compute_unflagged_eMLG = FALSE,
  distance_threshold = 5e5, cores = 2
)
```

```{r stage-500-plot, fig.height = 6.5}
p_500 <- plot_pruning_comparison(chr = "Chr1", stage1 = stage1,
                                 result = result_500kb, map = map, out_folder = tempdir())
p_500
```

In this small example the two limits give almost the same groups.

```{r dist-compare}
c(default_rho_derived = nrow(result$groups),
  fixed_500kb         = nrow(result_500kb$groups))
```

The flagged units inside a dense LD block already lie next to each other, so
the limit rarely matters, and widening it from a few kb to 500 kb bridges few
extra gaps. In the 500 kb plot the inversion looks like one green mass, but that
is because the colours repeat across hundreds of groups, and the number of
groups confirms that little changed. The limit matters much more for data with
*large* low-recombination blocks, such as megabase inversions or centromeric
regions. There a tight limit can leave a block split that a 500 kb limit would
consolidate.

Ideally the limit would be a **genetic** rather than a physical distance.
Supplying a `genetic_map` and one `cM_threshold` sets the limit in centimorgans.
Because a centimorgan spans *more* base pairs where recombination is suppressed,
a fixed limit in cM widens in base pairs exactly in the low-recombination regions
that hold the large LD blocks, and narrows elsewhere. No single fixed number of
base pairs can do this. No recombination map is bundled for these stickleback
data, so this example uses physical distance.

With physical distance, raising `dist_rho` widens the limit. The default of
0.95 gave a few kb above, and 0.99 gives a limit 5.2 times wider, because
`(0.99/0.01) / (0.95/0.05)` is 5.2.

```{r dist-099}
ds[, `:=`(rho_0.95_bp = round(d_from_rho(a_pred, 0.95)),
          rho_0.99_bp = round(d_from_rho(a_pred, 0.99)))]
ds[, .(Chr, rho_0.95_bp, rho_0.99_bp)]
```

Even at 0.99 the limit is only about 40 to 85 kb here, far short of 500 kb,
because LD decays fairly fast in these regions (`a_pred` about 1e-3 to 3e-3). A
500 kb limit at 0.99 would need about ten times slower decay (`a_pred` about
2e-4), which is typical of large low-recombination blocks such as the megabase
blocks in the *Formica* analysis. What 500 kb means therefore depends entirely on
the local decay rate. A limit in cM is the best choice where a map exists. The
limit derived from `dist_rho` for each chromosome is the next best because it
adapts to decay, and one fixed number of base pairs is the most convenient but
adapts least.

## Consensus fidelity and the flagging threshold

A Stage-1 unit is flagged for consolidation when its local LD support exceeds
`ld_w_threshold`, so a higher threshold flags fewer units. The consensus
fidelity `score_eMLG = cor(round(x), x)^2` measures whether a merged group's
consensus is still close to a discrete genotype, and `ld_prune_and_eMLG()` only
accepts a merge when it is at least 0.80. Varying the flagging threshold shows
the trade-off.

```{r sweep, results = "hide"}
TH <- c(0.025, 0.05, 0.1, 0.15)
fl <- rbindlist(lapply(TH, function(th) {
  r <- ld_prune_and_eMLG(GTs = GTs, stage1 = stage1, ld_w_col = "ld_w_095",
                         ld_w_threshold = th, score_threshold = 0.80, r2_th = 0.2,
                         LD_decay = ld_decay, dist_rho = 0.95, min_n_loci_flag = 5,
                         min_n_loci_eMLG = 5, compute_unflagged_eMLG = FALSE, cores = 2)
  g <- as.data.table(r$groups)[startsWith(group_id, "F")]
  g[, .(th = th, score, n_loci)]
}))
```

```{r fidelity-plot, fig.height = 6.5}
fl[, th_label := sprintf("ld_w threshold = %s  (n = %s, mean = %.3f)",
                         th, format(.N, big.mark = ","), mean(score)), by = th]
fl[, th_label := factor(th_label, levels = unique(th_label[order(th)]))]
fl[, cluster_type := fifelse(n_loci == 1, "singleton (no merge possible)", "merged (n_loci > 1)")]
hb <- fl[, { br <- seq(0.80, 1, by = 0.01); h <- hist(score, breaks = br, plot = FALSE)
             .(bin_mid = h$mids, count = h$counts) }, by = .(th_label, cluster_type)]
hb <- fl[, .(N = .N), by = th_label][hb, on = "th_label"][, pct := 100 * count / N]

ggplot(hb, aes(bin_mid, pct, fill = cluster_type)) +
  geom_col(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.1, width = 0.01) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.80, linetype = 2, colour = "#D08A45", linewidth = 0.5) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("singleton (no merge possible)" = "#C7CDD2",
                               "merged (n_loci > 1)" = "#315B7D"), name = NULL) +
  facet_wrap(~ th_label, ncol = 1) + coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0.80, 1)) +
  labs(x = expression(score[eMLG] == cor(round(x), x)^2),
       y = "% of that run's flagged units") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 9) +
  theme(legend.position = "top", strip.text = element_text(size = 7.5, face = "bold"))
```

Raising `ld_w_threshold` flags fewer units, but the units it leaves out are the
split units in extended LD that would benefit from merging. Lowering it adds
isolated single markers that have nothing to merge with, which form the peak at
the upper fidelity limit. The threshold decides *which units are considered*,
not which merges are accepted, because the fidelity and correlation limits
decide that. A low threshold therefore costs computing time rather than
accuracy.

```{r cleanup, include = FALSE}
SNPRelate::snpgdsClose(gds)
unlink(gds_path)
```

## Summary

On real stickleback data, this vignette estimated LD decay for each
chromosome, computed local LD support (`ld_w`) for each marker, grouped markers
into Stage-1 units and consolidated them into a pruned marker set and an eMLG
matrix. It also showed how the distance limit and the consensus fidelity affect
the consolidation. The window-level decay rate and the marker-level `ld_w`
agree on where the high-LD regions are.

The pruned marker set and the eMLG matrix can feed later LD-aware analyses,
such as building a GRM or association mapping. Outlier detection, which tests
the Stage-1 units directly, is covered in
`vignette("LDscnR_stage1_outlier_regions")`.
